text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The U.N. development report said AIDS had become Namibia's number one killer. It said 925 citizens died of the disease last year and one in every 15 people could be dying from it by the year 2001.
- The cabinet is exected to consider a proposal on how to proceed with plans to draw water from the Okavango river. A decision might be made by the end of the month.
- The U.N. development report said Namibia was marked by huge discrepancies between rich and poor. It also said AIDS and HIV could affect 300,000 people within the next four years.
- A fourth rare wild dog has been treated for serious injuries caused by snares in the Tsumkwe communal farming area.

- The president's office accused a Henties Bay resident of having personal gain as a motive in campaigning against Namibia's use of seal meat. A businessman in the same town has put his plans to process seal meat on hold, pending the outcome of an investigation.
